summary: Army veteran Marion Pettie founded the Finders, a Washington, DC commune run as a life-directing game, whose neglected children sparked a 1987 Satanic-panic trafficking scandal in Tallahassee and lasting rumours of CIA ties.

evidence.note: Pettie born in Culpeper, Virginia, December 1920
two decades in the Army, rising to master sergeant; drove Hap Arnold
followers gathered and group formally begun in 1971
game-caller structure: members ordered on spying missions, marriages, child rearing
communal child rearing and neglect of children born in the group
February 1987 arrest in Tallahassee of two men with six children
national media frenzy over devil-worship and abuse claims
unverified customs agent report fuels trafficking conspiracy lore
1993 reports of CIA computer training at a Finders-linked company
CIA Operation Chaos discussed as possible context for the group's spying
charges dropped after six weeks; children returned to mothers
Pettie dies in 2003; group lingers in Culpeper until then

notes: Hosts say 'Petty'; the standard spelling is Pettie, kept 'Marion Petty' as a keyword. Main span ends at the 1987 case; the 1990s Culpeper years and 1993 CIA revelations are in the covered span. QAnon/Pizzagate legacy is mentioned mainly in the intro and a short coda, so reaches_present is false. Child abuse is neglect plus unproven sexual-abuse allegations.
